The Guggenheim Museum Bilbao presents its ambitious and
diverse artistic program for 2026
Today, Friday, January 1 6, the Director General of the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao, Miren
Arzalluz , and the Museum's curatorial team unveiled the key elements of the seven exhibitions
that visitors can enjoy at the Museum throughout 2026. The new artistic program will begin on
March 19 with the first exhibition in Spain dedicated to the Japanese -American artist Ruth
Asawa, whose centenary is being celebrated this year. The program will continue on May 5 with
a new exhibition from the in situ series by South African artist Igshaan Adams, and the first half
of the year will culminat e in a comprehensive re trospective of the career of Jasper Johns, one
of the key figures in the art of the second half of the 20th century (sponsored by BBVA
Foundation ).

In autumn, starting October 1, the Film & Video gallery will host a striking work by Swiss artist
Pipilotti Rist. On October 9, an installation by London - based artist and filmmaker Steve
McQueen, sponsored by Occident, will open, and on November 12, a major exhibition
dedicated to New York artist Dan Flavin, drawn from the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum's
collection, will open in an ambitious presentation sponsored by Iberdrola. The last of the
temporary exhibitions for 2026 will be the second install ation fr om the in situ series , showcasing
the work of Korean - Canadian artist Zadie Xa.

In addition, throughout the year, visitors can enjoy the exhibition Works from the Guggenheim
Museum Bilbao Collection , sponsored by the BBK Banking Foundation and completely
renovated in November 2025. This exhibition presents a selection of works that highlight key
moments in the history of art after World War II and includes a large number of pieces recently

Guggenheim Museum's ...","relevance":"high","markdown":{"markdown":null,"code":"NOT_REQUESTED"},"highlights":{"highlights":["[The Guggenheim Museum Bilbao presents its ambitious and diverse artistic program for 2026]

Today, Friday, January 16, the Director General of the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao, Miren Arzalluz, and the Museum's curatorial team unveiled the key elements of the seven exhibitions that visitors can enjoy at the Museum throughout 2026. The new artistic program will begin on March 19 with the first exhibition in Spain dedicated to the Japanese-American artist Ruth Asawa, whose centenary is being celebrated this year. The program will continue on May 5 with a new exhibition from the *in situ* series by South African artist Igshaan Adams, and the first half of the year will culminate in a comprehensive retrospective of the career of Jasper Johns, one of the key figures in the art of the second half of the 20th century (sponsored by BBVA Foundation).

In autumn, starting October 1, the Film & Video gallery will host a striking work by Swiss artist Pipilotti Rist. On October 9, an installation by London-based artist and filmmaker Steve McQueen, sponsored by Occident, will open, and on November 12, a major exhibition dedicated to New York artist Dan Flavin, drawn from the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum's collection, will open in an ambitious presentation sponsored by Iberdrola. The last of the temporary exhibitions for 2026 will be the second installation from the *in situ* series, showcasing the work of Korean-Canadian artist Zadie Xa.

In addition, throughout the year, visitors can enjoy the exhibition *Works from the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao Collection*, sponsored by the BBK Banking Foundation and completely renovated in November 2025. This exhibition presents a selection of works that highlight key moments in the history of art after World War II and includes a large number of pieces recently added to the Collection."],"code":"SUCCESS"}},{"url":"https://www.guggenheim-bilbao.eus/en/exhibitions","title":"Exhibitions | Guggenheim Museum Bilbao","description":"ExhibitionWorks from the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao Collection · currentupcomingpast · Explore · Explore · Explore · Explore · 11.19.2026 - 04.11.2027","relevance":"high","markdown":{"markdown":null,"code":"NOT_REQUESTED"},"highlights":{"highlights":["[Exhibitions > Ever is Over All. The Guggenheim Museum Bilbao presents its ambitious and
diverse artistic program for 2026
Today, Friday, January 1 6, the Director General of the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao, Miren
Arzalluz , and the Museum's curatorial team unveiled the key elements of the seven exhibitions
that visitors can enjoy at the Museum throughout 2026. The new artistic program will begin on
March 19 with the first exhibition in Spain dedicated to the Japanese -American artist Ruth
Asawa, whose centenary is being celebrated this year. The program will continue on May 5 with
a new exhibition from the in situ series by South African artist Igshaan Adams, and the first half
of the year will culminat e in a comprehensive re trospective of the career of Jasper Johns, one
of the key figures in the art of the second half of the 20th century (sponsored by BBVA
Foundation ).

In autumn, starting October 1, the Film & Video gallery will host a striking work by Swiss artist
Pipilotti Rist. On October 9, an installation by London - based artist and filmmaker Steve
McQueen, sponsored by Occident, will open, and on November 12, a major exhibition
dedicated to New York artist Dan Flavin, drawn from the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum's
collection, will open in an ambitious presentation sponsored by Iberdrola. The last of the
temporary exhibitions for 2026 will be the second install ation fr om the in situ series , showcasing
the work of Korean - Canadian artist Zadie Xa.

In addition, throughout the year, visitors can enjoy the exhibition Works from the Guggenheim
Museum Bilbao Collection , sponsored by the BBK Banking Foundation and completely
renovated in November 2025. This exhibition presents a selection of works that highlight key
moments in the history of art after World War II and includes a large number of pieces recently
added to the Collection.

highlights:
[The Guggenheim Museum Bilbao presents its ambitious and diverse artistic program for 2026]

Today, Friday, January 16, the Director General of the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao, Miren Arzalluz, and the Museum's curatorial team unveiled the key elements of the seven exhibitions that visitors can enjoy at the Museum throughout 2026. The new artistic program will begin on March 19 with the first exhibition in Spain dedicated to the Japanese-American artist Ruth Asawa, whose centenary is being celebrated this year. The program will continue on May 5 with a new exhibition from the *in situ* series by South African artist Igshaan Adams, and the first half of the year will culminate in a comprehensive retrospective of the career of Jasper Johns, one of the key figures in the art of the second half of the 20th century (sponsored by BBVA Foundation).

In autumn, starting October 1, the Film & Video gallery will host a striking work by Swiss artist Pipilotti Rist. On October 9, an installation by London-based artist and filmmaker Steve McQueen, sponsored by Occident, will open, and on November 12, a major exhibition dedicated to New York artist Dan Flavin, drawn from the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum's collection, will open in an ambitious presentation sponsored by Iberdrola. The last of the temporary exhibitions for 2026 will be the second installation from the *in situ* series, showcasing the work of Korean-Canadian artist Zadie Xa.

In addition, throughout the year, visitors can enjoy the exhibition *Works from the Guggenheim Museum Bilbao Collection*, sponsored by the BBK Banking Foundation and completely renovated in November 2025. This exhibition presents a selection of works that highlight key moments in the history of art after World War II and includes a large number of pieces recently added to the Collection.

highlights:
[What to do in Madrid this summer 2026: discover the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum]

This summer, the Thyssen-Bornemisza National Museum brings together a diverse programme of exhibitions that bridges **tradition and contemporary art**. From the intimate vision of ***Carmen Laffón to Ewa Juszkiewicz’s reinterpretation of art history***, and from ***the restoration of Rubens’ Venus and Cupid to the immersive experience Forced to Hope***, there is something to inspire every visitor. The summer programme also includes activities such as ***Take Refuge in Culture***, which transforms the museum into a meeting place for dance and flamenco, as well as the ***Thyssen Terraces***, the perfect setting to enjoy art, gastronomy and summer evenings in the heart of Madrid.
